claim_under_attack.claim_text: The label data underlying this portfolio's ML claims is physically admissible.

corpora_audited.constraint_citation: Boyer, R.F., Rubber Chem. Technol. 36, 1303 (1963); Van Krevelen & Te Nijenhuis, 'Properties of Polymers', 4th ed., Elsevier 2009, ISBN 978-0-08-054819-7, Ch.6 (Tg/Tm ratio bounded in [0.5,0.8], i.e. Tg<Tm always for any real semicrystalline/amorphous polymer -- Tg is a kinetic freezing transition of the amorphous phase that occurs strictly below the true first-order crystalline melting transition).
corpora_audited.finding_summary: 24/167 (14.4%) OpenPoly rows with both Tg and Tm reported have Tg>=Tm, violating the Boyer-Beaman constraint that the glass transition (a kinetic freezing of the amorphous phase) must occur strictly below the true crystalline melting point. These 24 rows are training/validation examples inside the SAME openpoly_properties dataset_id (8de5baf76f79610f) consumed by 8 downstream KPIs, including the primary openpoly-experimental-tg-ml-baseline-kpi.v1.json Tg model.

corpora_audited.constraint: 0 < solubility_mole_fraction < 1, strict (a mole fraction is n_solute/(n_solute+n_solvent), a probability-like quantity bounded on the open unit interval by definition)
corpora_audited.constraint_citation: IUPAC Gold Book, 'amount fraction, mole fraction' (doi:10.1351/goldbook.A00296); definitional, not model-dependent.
corpora_audited.dependent_module_kpis_note: No amphora-molecule-property KPI receipt currently reads bigsoldb_solubility directly (grep of evidence/phase0/kpis/*.json and benchmarks/ found zero matches). The known downstream consumer of this corpus is amphora-solvent-property's Solvency BigSolDB result (LSO RMSE 0.877, that module's only externally-validated solvency claim) -- a different module, out of this fire's write scope, flagged here for cross-module awareness only.
corpora_audited.finding_summary: The primary physical bound (0<mole_fraction<1) is satisfied by all 103,944/103,944 rows -- no admissibility violation on that axis. However, a secondary, equally physical check -- do repeated measurements of the same (solute, solvent, temperature) triple agree with each other -- found 4,134/4,578 (90.3%) of duplicate-measurement groups disagree by more than 0.3 log10(mol/L) units (>2x) at IDENTICAL conditions. A single physical quantity cannot have two internally-contradictory literature values at the same state point; this is a corpus-level admissibility defect distinct from (and larger in count than) a simple out-of-bounds check would catch.

secondary_diagnostic_internal_log10_cons.note: NOT part of the admissible/pct gate above -- reported separately as a data-integrity cross-check.

corpora_audited.constraint: 0.6 g/cm^3 <= liquid density <= 3.4 g/cm^3 at near-ambient conditions
corpora_audited.constraint_citation: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 104th ed. (2023), ISBN 978-1-032-63111-2, Section 'Physical Constants of Organic Compounds' -- common liquid organic solvents span from n-pentane (0.626 g/cm^3) to dense halogenated liquids such as diiodomethane (3.325 g/cm^3); densities outside this band indicate either a unit/transcription error or a non-liquid/non-organic-solvent entry.
corpora_audited.dependent_module_kpis_note: Same cross-module caveat as bigsoldb_solubility above; consumed by amphora-solvent-property, not this module's KPIs.
corpora_audited.finding_summary: 2209/2210 (99.95%) rows fall within the physically-plausible organic-liquid density band [0.6, 3.4] g/cm^3. Essentially clean; 1 row flagged for manual review.

constraint_A_frohlich.constraint_citation: Frohlich, H., 'Theory of Dielectrics', Oxford University Press, 1949, Ch.2 -- static permittivity eps_static(omega->0) sums electronic+ionic+orientational polarization and must be >= the optical/electronic-only permittivity eps_inf=n^2 (Maxwell relation) for any passive linear dielectric.
constraint_A_frohlich.name: eps_static >= n_refractive^2 (Frohlich inequality)
constraint_A_frohlich.note: This is the SAME constraint applied to radonpy_pi1070 (1077 rows, C8 fires 1-3, 113/1075=10.5% admissible). polyomics_small_molecules is the larger raw RadonPy simulation-output corpus (28159 rows) that PI1070 was curated from; this generalizes the prior finding to see whether it is an artifact of the 1070-row curation or persists at full scale.

constraint_B_refractive_index_lower_boun.constraint_citation: Lorentz-Lorenz theory (H.A. Lorentz 1880; L. Lorenz 1880); for any condensed-phase dielectric medium in the normal (non-anomalous) dispersion regime at optical frequencies, refractive index relative to vacuum n>=1 by definition of phase velocity v=c/n<=c.
constraint_B_refractive_index_lower_boun.name: refractive_index >= 1

corpora_audited.finding_summary: This is the larger raw RadonPy simulation-output corpus (28,159 rows) that the already-audited radonpy_pi1070 (1,077 rows, C8 fires 1-3) was curated from. Applying the SAME Frohlich inequality (eps_static>=n^2) at full scale finds 16,990/27,964 (60.8%) admissible -- i.e. 39.2% violate, NOT the 89.5% violation rate found in the curated PI1070 subset. The two numbers disagree by a factor of >2x in violation rate. This means PI1070's curation step specifically concentrated (not merely inherited) the dielectric-admissibility defect relative to the raw simulation dump it was drawn from -- a new finding this fire surfaces that C8 could not see from PI1070 alone. Separately, the refractive-index lower bound (n>=1, Lorentz-Lorenz) is essentially clean at full scale: 27,963/27,964 (99.996%) admissible.

cross_corpus_summary.headline: The portfolio-wide claim 'the label data underlying this portfolio's ML claims is physically admissible' does NOT hold uniformly. Beyond the already-refuted RadonPy PI1070 dielectric case (C8), this audit finds: (1) OpenPoly Tg/Tm violates a basic polymer-thermodynamics ordering constraint in 14.4% of evaluable rows, feeding 8 downstream KPIs including the primary Tg ML baseline; (2) BigSolDB solubility, while clean on its primary mole-fraction bound, has internally CONTRADICTORY repeated measurements in 90.3% of its duplicate-measurement groups; (3) the raw RadonPy simulation dump (polyomics_small_molecules) shows the same Frohlich-inequality defect as PI1070 but at a materially different rate (39.2% vs 89.5%), revealing that PI1070's curation concentrated the defect rather than merely inheriting it. Only BigSolDB density and the RadonPy refractive-index axis are clean (>99.9%).

method: For each corpus, read the normalized JSONL-gz rows directly from the shared data lake at feedback/v2/normalized/<acquisition_unit_id>.jsonl.gz (the same files this module's manifests at reference/mvp20/manifests/*.json point to via normalized_path/normalized_sha256), apply one or more physical/definitional constraints independent of any ML model, and count admissible vs inadmissible rows. No quarantined or CONTEXT_ONLY source was opened; all four corpora carry rights_class=DERIVATIVE_ALLOWED per their feedback_v2/rights/*.json manifests.
objective: Audit >=4 in-tree corpora for physical-admissibility violations in their ground-truth label columns, quantify n_total/n_admissible/pct per corpus, cite the physical justification for each constraint, and list which downstream module KPIs depend on the flagged rows.
prior_fire_context: W2 fire 1 (receipt sha256=1bead43f720612933ef00d738018a587d31d1a22d1c00c6901073640b7c4ea32) generalized the C8 RadonPy-dielectric physical-admissibility audit (eps_static>=n^2) to 4 in-tree corpora: OpenPoly Tg/Tm ordering (Boyer-Beaman), BigSolDB solubility mole-fraction bound + duplicate-measurement contradiction check, BigSolDB density band, and the raw RadonPy polyomics_small_molecules corpus (Frohlich inequality + refractive-index lower bound) at 26x PI1070's scale. Fire 1's science, refutation criterion, and two-replay gate were all correct, but the receipt was signed with the repo-local LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT_AUDIT_ONLY dev key (key_id=local-9028773f49591193), which is explicitly NOT present in config/phase0-trust-store.v1.json. The launcher rejected that verdict: verified_new_signed=0, because a DECLARED artifact must pass real Ed25519 DSSE verification against the pinned Phase-0 trust-store key. This fire does not repeat or extend the audit -- it re-derives the identical findings from fire 1 (carried forward verbatim, cited by sha256) into a new receipt, signed with the phase0-internal-reviewer key confirmed present at /home/ubuntu/.local/share/amphora/phase0/keys/ and registered in the trust store with phase0_authorized=true, revoked=false.
promotion_blocked_by: NOT this audit's science (all gates pass) and NOT key custody (trust-anchored key now used). Manifest untouched at 66/11. Module promotion still requires 2 human dual-identity ceremony keys this cron does not hold, per standing governance.
recommended_followups: openpoly-experimental-tg-ml-baseline-kpi.v1.json and the 7 other dependent KPIs should be re-run with the 24 Tg>=Tm rows excluded from train/calib/test to determine whether the shipped Tg MAE is inflated by these physically-inadmissible examples (same escalation pattern as C8 fire 2).

File a data-acquisition/rights-review ask for BigSolDB: the 90.3% duplicate-contradiction rate means the corpus needs a reconciliation policy (e.g. keep only single-source or median-of-agreeing-sources measurements) before amphora-solvent-property's Solvency BigSolDB KPI (RMSE 0.877, its only ext-validated claim) can be considered clean at the label level -- this is cross-module and out of this fire's write scope, but is the single highest-leverage follow-up this audit surfaces.

Investigate WHY PI1070's curation concentrated the Frohlich-inequality defect (89.5% violation) relative to the raw polyomics_small_molecules dump it was drawn from (39.2% violation) -- if the curation criterion correlates with simulation non-convergence, that same non-convergence flag could be used as a cheap admissibility pre-filter across the whole polyomics_small_molecules corpus for future RadonPy-derived KPIs.
refutation_criterion: Pre-registered: the claim survives only if ALL >=4 audited corpora show >=95% admissible rows on their respective physical constraints. Observed: 2 of 4 corpora fall well below this bar (openpoly_properties 85.6%, polyomics_small_molecules Frohlich axis 60.8%), and a 5th diagnostic axis (BigSolDB duplicate-contradiction rate) shows 90.3% internal contradiction. Criterion fired -- claim REFUTED.
